data.body:
RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1 complete) — the ticket's stated cause is REJECTED; the real mechanism is module-identity duplication.

REJECTED hypothesis: 'cwd/tracker_dir resolution leaks so os.path.isdir(_config.tracker_dir()) is False'. Runtime probe under the exact failing order shows tracker_dir() = <tmp>/repo/.tickets-tracker and isdir=True. The sweep is not skipped by the isdir guard at all.

PROVEN root cause: tests/unit/test_ensures_late_binding.py leaves a DUPLICATE rebar._store.ensures module bound on its parent package.
- That test does sys.modules.pop('rebar._store.ensures'), then importlib.import_module(...) inside a MonkeyPatch context to reproduce the d720-fc72 import-time capture window.
- importlib rebinds the parent-package attribute (setattr(rebar._store, 'ensures', <new module>)) as part of loading a submodule.
- Its finally block restores sys.modules ONLY. rebar._store.ensures is left pointing at the fresh module object.
- 'from rebar._store import ensures' resolves via getattr(package, 'ensures') (IMPORT_FROM falls back to sys.modules only on AttributeError), so every LATER such import in that process gets the NEW module, while sys.modules still holds the ORIGINAL.

How that produces ['run']:
- tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_ensures.py binds 'ensures' at module import (collection) time -> the ORIGINAL object.
- monkeypatch.setattr(ensures, 'run_ensures', _fake_run_ensures) therefore patches the ORIGINAL.
- mcp_server.main() does a function-LOCAL 'from rebar._store import ensures as _ensures' (src/rebar/mcp_server.py:714) at call time -> the NEW, UNPATCHED module. The real run_ensures runs (harmlessly, against the fixture tracker), appends nothing, and order == ['run'].

Runtime proof (probe): sys.modules['rebar._store.ensures'] id=4500430160 (== the collect-time binding) but rebar._store.ensures id=4500437040 -> 'identical: False'.

Deterministic reproduction (this is the exact CI assertion, not a lookalike):
  python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_ensures_late_binding.py tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_ensures.py::test_mcp_startup_sweeps_before_run
  -> AssertionError: assert ['run'] == ['ensures', 'run']

Why it is order-dependent: default collection sorts tests/interfaces before tests/unit, so locally the target runs first and passes. CI parallelises with pytest-xdist (.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:620, '-n' pinned), and load-balancing can put the unit polluter earlier in the same worker. (Note: this repo has no pytest-randomly dependency at all — the ticket's attribution to pytest-randomly is incorrect; the order source is xdist work distribution.)

Defect legitimacy: defect. The polluter's own finally block exists to restore module state, and tests/conftest.py's block_extra fixture documents the project invariant that 'the global import state never leaks across tests (incl. under pytest-xdist)'. The restore is simply incomplete.

Defect origin: commit 1496adf2b2 'ensures: late-bind lock.canonical_tracker' (2026-08-21), ticket d720-fc72-3763-4cac, which introduced tests/unit/test_ensures_late_binding.py — the only test in the suite that pops a rebar submodule from sys.modules and re-imports it. Date test passes: the target test predates it (test_fsck_ensures.py last touched f1db672ecd) and the polluter file did not exist before. Class: regression.
